title: sre-oncall-scratchpad-jordan-2026-03-13
content:
Daily on-call scratchpad - informal notes and todo list

Date: 2026-03-13
Oncall: Jordan Kim (primary)
Backup: Priya Nair
Shift: 09:00-17:00 PT

Summary of pages this shift:
- 03:14 UTC: PD page PD-incident-1387 - svc-cache high error rate -> 503s for public-hosted route /v1/generate. Linked to downstream retry storm from edge rollback.
- 04:02 UTC: Follow-up alert - increased eviction rate on redis-inference-cache-02. Evictions spiked ~200% during 03:10-03:30 window.

What I did (timeline rough):
- 03:16 UTC: Acked page, posted to #sre-oncall with initial triage. Grabbed logs from runtime-proxy and redis metrics.
- 03:20 UTC: Noted many 502/503s returned by runtime-proxy with upstream 524 (timeout to model-workers).
- 03:24 UTC: Scaled up model-worker ASG (temp burst) by +2 instances via runbook command. Confirmed new workers registered to router by 03:31.
- 03:32 UTC: Error rate dropped from 18% -> 3% over next 6 minutes.
- 03:40 UTC: Observed persistent tail latency increase on calls hitting long-context Llama-70b-q4a. Digging into KV-cache miss rate.

Immediate hypothesis:
- Root cause: cascade from edge rollback (old traffic mix) causing sudden higher concurrency to a subset of model workers with cold KV cache, causing timeouts and triggering rapid client retries -> overload + redis thrash (evictions).
- Contributing: cache eviction policy on redis-inference-cache-02 is aggressive under OOM; no graceful fallback. Router does not detect degraded worker profiles (high cpu/long latency) to re-route.

New/interesting signals:
- redis-inference-cache-02 had large keys (~1.4MB) from a malformed batch request; that correlated with memory pressure. Need to add sanitizer upstream.
- model-worker logs show repeated "kv_load_timeout" messages at ~50ms. Kernel-level metrics show CPU steal low, so likely worker thread starvation from GC/compaction on large tensors (quantized ops).

Runbook TODOs / follow-ups (actionable):
- [ ] Update runbook section "cache-eviction-mitigation" to include command to temporarily switch route to fallback-cache cluster. (owner: Jordan)
- [ ] Create JIRA SRE-4523 to track adding a per-request key-size validator in runtime-proxy to drop overly large cache keys and return 413 instead of letting them populate redis. (owner: Priya)
- [ ] Add heatmap to dashboard for key size distribution per minute (Grafana panel). (owner: Luca)
- [ ] Add router heuristic to mark workers as degraded by 95th pct latency + kv_load_timeout ratio to avoid routing new sessions. (owner: eng-serving-runtime team -> link to PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2791)
- [ ] Postmortem draft (initial notes) and timeline - due EOD tomorrow. Start skeleton and assign: Jordan (write), Priya (metrics), Luca (graphs).
- [ ] Add automated alert: redis_eviction_rate > 5/s sustained for 5m + p50 latency increase > 2x -> page SRE and mute non-urgent repo watchers. (owner: eng-observability)

Notes to self / things I want to remember:
- When paging for cache-related 503s, check for one "big key" pattern: repeated key prefix 'user-session:' + very long prompt blob. This was present in logs at 03:12:55.
- Keep a copy of the runtime-proxy command used to scale ASG: "./infractl scale-asg model-workers --add 2 --reason \"oncall emergency 2026-03-13\"" (put in personal runbook snippets).
- Confirmed scaling helped but didn't fully mitigate: need both scaling + smarter routing to avoid repeated retries flooding redis.

Post-incident notes for handoff:
- Hand off to Priya at 17:00 PT. Leave checklist completed items and open tickets in this doc. Priya to coordinate postmortem and customer comms for affected hosted API customers (cc: solutions-eng).

Open questions / uncertainties:
- Did the edge rollback trigger originate from deployment pipeline? Need to check release engineering logs (possible bad rollout at 03:05). Link placeholder: confluence:redwood/release/logs-2026-03-13
- Is there a safe short-term config for redis maxmemory-policy that favors LRU over volatile-lru for our workload? Test needed in staging.

Misc scraps / quick commands used:
- tail -n 200 /var/log/runtime-proxy/2026-03-13.log | grep \"kv_load_timeout\"
- redis-cli -h redis-inference-cache-02 INFO memory | egrep 'used_memory_human|evicted_keys'
- kubectl get pods -n runtime | grep model-worker | xargs -I{} kubectl top pod {} -n runtime

Meeting / follow-up schedule:
- 2026-03-13 19:00 PT: Quick 30m sync with eng-serving-runtime to propose router heuristic change. Invite: Priya, Luca, Maya (runtime owner).
- 2026-03-14 11:00 PT: Postmortem dry-run review.

Tags for search: oncall, cache, redis, kv-cache, runtime-proxy, incident-1387

Free-form thoughts (brain dump):
- We rely a lot on scaling to absorb short spikes; that's ok but masking a design issue where single large keys can destabilize cache clusters. Could consider enforcing per-key hard limits at the proxy.
- Long-term: evaluate per-tenant resource shaping to prevent noisy neighbors from affecting shared cache.

End of scratchpad.

-- Jordan
